# Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 22, 2026

## Toplines

**The Russian Ministry of Defense (MoD) falsely claimed that Russian forces have encircled Dobropillya — an intensification of the Kremlin’s cognitive warfare campaign alleging encirclements across various sectors of the frontline to falsely present Ukrainian defenses as collapsing**. The Russian MoD claimed on September 22 that the Russian Central Grouping of Forces encircled Dobropillya and are advancing toward Oleksandrivka (northwest of Dobropillya).\[1\] The MoD’s vague statement notably did not include a map or any evidence to support these false claims. ISW has observed no evidence to support the Russian MoD’s encirclement claims, which are incompatible with recent Ukrainian statements. The chief of staff of a Ukrainian artillery reconnaissance battalion stated on September 22 that Russian forces have not made major advances in the Dobropillya direction and that the Russian military command frequently postpones its own deadlines due to heavy personnel casualties and inconsistencies between its plans and the battlefield realities.\[2\] Ukrainian military observer Kostyantyn Mashovets stated on September 20 that Ukrainian forces maintain positions south and northeast of Dobropillya.\[3\]

![Map Thumbnail](https://understandingwar.org/map/assessed-control-of-terrain-in-the-dobropillya-tactical-area-september-22-2026-at-130-pm-et/ "Assessed Control of Terrain in the Dobropillya Tactical Area, September 22, 2026 at 1:30 PM ET")

**The Kremlin is likely intensifying its encirclement claims against the backdrop of the ongoing UN General Assembly (UNGA) session and recent Ukrainian successes on the northern flank of the Fortress Belt.** Russian military officials have repeatedly made false claims about the encirclement of Ukrainian forces, including in Kursk Oblast in October 2024, in Kupyansk in Fall and Winter 2025-2026, and in the Rubtsi direction (northwest of Lyman) in June 2026.\[4\] The Russian MoD and Russian milbloggers have most recently claimed an encirclement of Ukrainian forces in northeastern Ukraine between the Velykyi Burluk and Vovchansk directions.\[5\] The Russian MoD is likely proliferating its claims of encirclement now to support Russian diplomatic engagements at the September 21-28 UNGA session that will aim to push for Ukrainian capitulation to end the war.

The Russian MoD’s latest claim about Dobropillya also comes as Ukrainian forces have eliminated the Russian salient north of Lyman in recent months, forcing the Russian military command to rethink its wider plans to use Russian offensive activity in the Lyman and Dobropillya directions to conduct a wide encirclement of the Fortress Belt and all of Donetsk Oblast.\[6\] The MoD’s false claim of an encirclement around Dobropillya aims in part to divert attention from these recent Ukrainian successes.

**Russian authorities are reportedly training some regional government officials for possible mobilization scenarios.** The Udmurt Republic will hold a two-day long “Organization of Mobilization Training in State and Local Government Bodies” training program for 20 state and municipal employees.\[7\] The program will reportedly run until December 5, and its modules will include lessons about the transition of the Russian economy to wartime conditions, the organization of mobilization planning, the military registration of citizens in the reserves, the protection of classified information, and the monitoring of mobilization preparations. The Udmurt Republic has reportedly held these training sessions before, but the program comes amid increasing indications that the Kremlin may conduct some form of mobilization in the near future and indicates that Russian authorities are preparing regional civil servants and government employees for the administrative and economic challenges inherent in mobilization.\[8\] The increasing Russian casualty rate and declining volunteer recruitment rate will likely force Russian President Vladimir Putin to order some form of mobilization in the near future to continue the current tempo of Russian offensive operations in Ukraine.\[9\] It is still unclear, however, if Putin has made a final decision about conducting a mobilization and, if he has, what kind of mobilization he will order. The Kremlin has heavily targeted Russian federal subjects with large ethnic minority groups like the Udmurt Republic for contract recruitment and covert force generation in recent years.\[10\] The Kremlin may attempt to minimize public backlash regarding a future mobilization by concentrating recruitment efforts in these regions while insulating wealthier and politically significant areas such as Moscow and Leningrad oblasts.

**Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and US President Donald Trump expressed their willingness to end the war in Ukraine during a September 22 joint press conference on the sidelines of UNGA.** Zelensky expressed hope that Trump could help end the war in Ukraine before the upcoming winter.\[11\] Trump stated that Russia and Ukraine “are going to make a deal” but did not announce specifics. Trump also noted that Ukraine’s long-range strike campaign against Russian oil refineries has “dealt a serious blow” to Russia’s diesel industry. Zelensky told journalists, after his closed meeting with Trump, that the United States will convey Ukraine’s proposal for a ceasefire of long-range strikes on energy infrastructure to Russia and noted his opennessfor a trilateral meeting with Trump and Putin.\[12\]

## Key Takeaways

1. The Russian Ministry of Defense (MoD) falsely claimed that Russian forces have encircled Dobropillya — an intensification of the Kremlin’s cognitive warfare campaign alleging encirclements across various sectors of the frontline to falsely present Ukrainian defenses as collapsing.
2. The Kremlin is likely intensifying its encirclement claims against the backdrop of the ongoing UN General Assembly (UNGA) session and recent Ukrainian successes on the northern flank of the Fortress Belt.
3. Russian authorities are reportedly training some regional government officials for possible mobilization scenarios.
4. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and US President Donald Trump expressed their willingness to end the war in Ukraine during a September 22 joint press conference on the sidelines of UNGA.
5. Neither Ukrainian nor Russian forces advanced on September 22.
6. Russia launched 212 drones and an unspecified number of missiles against Ukraine overnight.
7. Ukrainian forces continued their long-range drone strike campaign against Russian oil refineries on September 21 and 22.

![Map Thumbnail](https://understandingwar.org/map/assessed-control-of-terrain-in-the-russo-ukrainian-war-september-22-2026-at-130-pm-et/ "Assessed Control of Terrain in the Russo-Ukrainian War, September 22, 2026 at 1:30 PM ET")

_We do not report in detail on Russian war crimes because these activities are well-covered in Western media and do not directly affect the military operations we are assessing and forecasting. We will continue to evaluate and report on the effects of these criminal activities on the Ukrainian military and the Ukrainian population and specifically on combat in Ukrainian urban areas. We utterly condemn Russian violations of the laws of armed conflict and the Geneva Conventions and crimes against humanity even though we do not describe them in these reports._

## Ukrainian Operations in the Russian Federation

**Ukrainian forces continued their long-range strike campaign against Russian oil refineries on September 21 and 22.** The Ukrainian General Staff reported that Ukrainian forces struck the Bashneft-UNPZ Oil Refinery in Ufa, Republic of Bashkortostan (roughly 1,338 kilometers from the international border) and the Kuibyshev Oil Refinery in Samara City (roughly 920 kilometers from the international border) on September 21 or overnight on September 21 to 22, causing fires at both facilities.\[13\] The Ukrainian General Staff stated that the Bashneft-UNPZ Oil Refinery has aprocessing capacity of around 7.5 million tons of oil per year and that the Kuibyshev Oil Refinery has a processing capacity of around 7 million tons of oil per year. Geolocated footage published on September 22 shows smoke plumes and fires at the Kuibyshev Oil Refinery.\[14\] Ukrainian defense source Militarnyi reported that satellite imagery and footage indicate that Ukrainian strikes on the Kuibyshev Oil Refinery damaged its AVT-5 primary processing unit.\[15\] Zelensky also stated that Ukrainian forces struck unspecified targets in the Black Sea on September 22.\[16\]

**Ukrainian strikes against Russian oil infrastructure continue to constrain Russia’s oil processing capabilities.** Three industry sources told Reuters on September 21 that the Gazpromneft-Moscow Oil Refinery halted crude oil processing following the September 20 Ukrainian drone strikes against the refinery.\[17\] The sources stated that the Ukrainian strikes caused fires at the refinery’s primary crude distillation units and that repairs could take several weeks.

**The Ukrainian General Staff provided an updated battlefield damage assessment (BDA) of a recent Ukrainian strike against Oryol Oblast.** The Ukrainian General Staff confirmed on September 22 that the Ukrainian strike against a Russian drone storage, preparation, and launch site near Tsymbulova, Oryol Oblast (roughly 173 kilometers from the international border), on September 21 damaged at least three drone storage facilities, a jet-powered drone launch pad, and five drone launchers.\[18\]

## Russian Supporting Effort: Northern Axis

#### **Russian objective: Create defensible buffer zones in Sumy Oblast along the international border**

**Russian forces recently conducted an infiltration mission east of Sumy City.** Ukrainian forces struck Russian servicemembers east of Velykyi Prykil (east of Sumy City), according to geolocated footage published on September 22, after what ISW assesses was a Russian infiltration mission.\[19\]

**Russian forces continue to conduct glide bomb strikes against frontline settlements in northern Sumy Oblast to set conditions for future offensives.** Russian forces conducted a FAB-1500 glide bomb strike against a Ukrainian position in Khotin (north of Sumy City), according to geolocated footage published on September 21.\[20\] A Russian milblogger claimed on September 22 that Russian forces are advancing near Khotin.\[21\] Russian forces often conduct glide bomb strikes against settlements in the near rear, in part to create ruins that Russian infantry can use for cover and concealment during subsequentoffensive operations.\[22\]

![Map Thumbnail](https://understandingwar.org/map/assessed-control-of-terrain-in-the-sumy-direction-september-22-2026-at-130-pm-et/ "Assessed Control of Terrain in the Sumy Direction, September 22, 2026 at 1:30 PM ET")

**Russian forces continue efforts to use infiltration missions to establish a “buffer zone” in northern Sumy and Kharkiv oblasts.** Ukrainian Joint Forces Group Spokesperson Colonel Viktor Trehubov reported on September 20 that Russian forces maintain positions in a narrow strip of territory in the Sumy Oblast border areas, particularly near Hrabovske (southeast of Sumy City) and are conducting infiltration missions in border areas in the Vovchansk, Velykyi Burluk, and Hrabovske directions in an attempt to establish a continuous barrier along the international border.\[23\] Trehubov noted that Russian claims that Russian forces have adva
